questions.q: The number of 6-letter words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using the letters of the word MATHS such that any letter that appears in the word must appear at least twice, is _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
(i) Single letter is used, then no. of words $=5$
(ii) Two distinct letters are used, then no. of words
${ }^5 \mathrm{C}_2 \times\left(\frac{6!}{2!4!} \times 2+\frac{6!}{3!3!}\right)=10(30+20)=500$
(iii) Three distinct letters are used, then no. of words
${ }^5 \mathrm{C}_3 \times \frac{6!}{2!2!2!}=900$ Total no. of words $=1405$

questions.q: Some couples participated in a mixed doubles badminton tournament. If the number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match, is $840$, then the total numbers of persons, who participated in the tournament, is ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Some couples participated in a mixed doubles badminton tournament. If the number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match, is $840$,

Now Let total number of persons be $2n$, so number of couples will be~$n$

Now~number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match is given by,

$⇒ C2 n \cdot C2 n - 2 \cdot 2 = 840$

{as if we choose couple as \left\{A, B\right\}$~and other couple as~\left\{C, D\right\}$~and taking other two couple as~\left\{x, y\right\} \text{ and } \left\{w, z\right\}$, so the possible combination of the match~ where no couple played in a match will be,~\left\{A, x\right\} \to \left\{C, w\right\} \text{ and } \left\{C, x\right\} \to \left\{A, w\right\}$,~hence there are two possible combination after choosing~}

$⇒ n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) = 5 \cdot 6 \cdot 7 \cdot 8$

So,~$n = 8$

Hence, the number of persons will be,~$2n = 16$

questions.q: Let $S$~be the set of all passwords which are six to eight characters long, where each character is either an alphabet from \left\{A, B, C, D, E\right\}$ or a number from \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\}$ with the repetition of characters allowed. If the number of passwords in $S$ whose at least one character is a number from \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\}$ is $\alpha \times {5}^{6}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given total available characters is& $10$~and total digits are~$5$,

So, for$6 -$digit password, the~number of ways $= {10}^{6} - {5}^{6}$

For~$7 -$digit~password, the~number of ways $= {10}^{7} - {5}^{7}$

For $8 -$digit password, the number of ways $= {10}^{8} - {5}^{8}$

$∴$~ Total ways $= \left({10}^{6} + {10}^{7} + {10}^{8}\right) - \left({5}^{6} + {5}^{7} + {5}^{8}\right)

$= {2}^{6}{5}^{6} + {2}^{7}{5}^{7} + {2}^{8}{5}^{8} - {5}^{6} - {5}^{7} - {5}^{8}$

$= {5}^{6}\left({2}^{6} +$5 $\cdot {2}^{7} +$25 $\cdot {2}^{8} -$1 - 5 - 25\right) = 7073 $\cdot {5}^{6}

Now on comparing with~\alpha \times {5}^{6}~we get~\alpha =$7073$

questions.q: There are $15$ players in a cricket team, out of which $6$ are bowlers, $7$ are batsmen and $2$ are wicketkeepers. The number of ways, a team of $11$~players be selected from them so as to include at least $4$ bowlers, $5$ batsmen and $1$ wicketkeeper, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$15:$ Players

$6:$ Bowlers

$7:$ Batsman

$2:$ Wicket keepers

Total number of ways for at least $4$ bowlers, $5$ batsman and~$1$~wicket keeper

$= \left(C4 6 \times C6 7 \times C1 2\right) + \left(C4 6 \timesC5 7 \timesC2 2\right) + \left(C5 6 \timesC5 7 \timesC1 2\right)$

$= 777

$

questions.q: The largest natural number $n$ such that $3n$ divides~$66 !$~is~_______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that,

Maximum value& of& $n$~for~$p^{n}$~where~$p$~is prime~divides the number~$a !$~is given by,

~\left[\dfrac{a}{p}\right] + \left[\dfrac{a}{p2}\right] + \left[\dfrac{a}{p3}\right] + \left[\dfrac{a}{p4}\right] + . . .$

Since,~$3$~is a prime number, so we have

$= \left[\dfrac{66}{3}\right] + \left[\dfrac{66}{32}\right] + \left[\dfrac{66}{33}\right] + \left[\dfrac{66}{34}\right] + . . .$

$= 22 + 7 + 2 + 0$

$= 31$

So, maximum value of~$n$~is~$31$.

$

questions.q: For $\mathrm{n} \geq 2$, let $S_n$ denote the set of all subsets of $\{1,2 \ldots . . ., n\}$ with no two consecutive numbers. For example $\{1,3,5\} \in \mathrm{S}_6$, but $\{1,2,4\} \notin \mathrm{S}_6$. Then n \left(\mathrm{~S}}_{5}\right) is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5 \ldots . . . \mathrm{n}\}$
No. of subsets having $r$ elements such that no two are consecutive is $={ }^{n-r+1} C_r$
for $\mathrm{n}=5$, no. of ways $={ }^{6 \cdot \mathrm{r}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}$
Subsets having no element $=1$
Subsets having exactly 1 element $={ }^5 \mathrm{C}_1=5$
Subsets having exactly 2 element $={ }^4 \mathrm{C}_2=6$
Subsets having exactly 3 element $={ }^3 \mathrm{C}_3=1$
$\Rightarrow 5+6+1+1=13$

questions.q: In an examination, $5$ students have been allotted their seats as per their roll numbers. The number of ways, in which none of the students sits on the allotted seat, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$5$~boys with allotted roll numbers and seat numbers are seated in such a way that no one sits on the allotted seats. The number of ways of such seating arrangement is equal to the derangement of~$5$~boys i.e.,

$= 5 ! \left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{1 !} + \dfrac{1}{2 !} - \dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} - \dfrac{1}{5 !}\right)

$= 5 ! - 5 ! + 60 - 20 + 5 - 1$

$= 44$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
& Consonants are& $L, T, T, R$

Vowels are~$E, E,$

Total number of words (without meaning) from letters of word~$' LETTER ' = \dfrac{6 !}{2 ! 2 !} = 180$

questions.q: Suppose Anil's mother wants to give $5$~whole fruits to Anil from a basket of $7$ red apples, $5$ white apples and $8$ oranges. If in the selected $5$ fruits, at least $2$ orange, at least one red apple and at least one white apple must be given, then the number of ways, Anil's mother can offer $5$ fruits to Anil is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$7$ Red apple \left(RA\right)$

$5$ white apple \left(WA\right)$

$8$ oranges \left(O\right)$

Now, for offering~$5$ fruits to be selected~

Possible selections :- $( 2O$, $1RA$, $2WA )$ or \left(2O, 2RA, 1WA\right)$, ~or \left(3O, 1RA, 1WA\right)$

Required number of ways

$= C2 8 C1 7 C2 5 + C2 8 C2 7 C1 5 + C3 8 C1 7 C1 5$

$= 1960 + 2940 + 1960$

$= 6860$

$

questions.q: The sum of all $3$-digit numbers less than or equal to $500,$ that are formed without using the digit $1$~and they all are multiple of $11,$& is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$209, 220, 231, . . . . . . . . , 495$ series in A.P.

Clearly,~$a = 209, d = 220 - 209 = 11$~and~$l = 495$

Where~$a$~is the first term,~$d$~is the common difference and~$l$~is the last term.

$⇒ l = a + \left(n - 1\right)d = 495$

where~$n$~is the number of terms

$⇒ l = 209 + \left(n - 1\right)11 = 495$

$⇒ \left(n - 1\right)11 = 286$

$⇒ \left(n - 1\right) = 26$

$⇒ n = 27$

Sum$= \dfrac{27}{2}\left(2 \times 209 + \left(26\right) \times 11\right)= 27\left(209 + 143\right) = 27 \times 352 = 9504$

Numbers containing~$1$~at unit place $= 231, 341, 451$

Numbers containing $1$~at ${10}^{th}$~place $= 319, 418$

Hence, required sum of all~$3$-digit~numbers less than or equal to~$500= 9501 - \left(231 + 341 + 451 + 319 + 418\right) = 7744$

questions.q: All the letters of the word $GTWENTY$ are written in all possible ways with or without meaning and these words are written as in a dictionary. The serial number of the word $GTWENTY$ IS
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have to find the rank of word $GTWENTY$.

Words starting from $E= \dfrac{6 !}{2 !} = \dfrac{720}{2} = 360$

Words starting with $GE = \dfrac{5 !}{2} = 60$

Words starting with $GN = \dfrac{5 !}{2} = 60$

Words starting with $GTE = 4 ! = 24$

Words starting with $GTN = 4 ! = 24$

Words starting with $GTT = 4 ! = 24$

Then the next word will be $GTWENTY$ and its rank will be $360 + 60 + 60 + 24 + 24 + 24 + 1 = 553$

questions.q: The total number of three-digit numbers, with one digit repeated exactly two times, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For three digit number we have following cases,

Case I: When digit zero is repeated

Number of numbers $= C1 9 = 9$

Case II: When digit zero is present but not repeated

Number of numbers $= C1 9 \cdot 2 ! = 18$

Case III: When digit zero is not present

Number of numbers $= 9 \cdot 8 \cdot \dfrac{3 !}{2 !} = 216$

Total number of numbers $= 243$

questions.q: The total number of $3$-digit numbers, whose greatest common divisor with~$36$ is $2$, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Prime factorisation of& $36 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3$

So, for number having G.C.D with $36$~to be~$2$, the number should be odd multiple of~$2$~and does not have~factor~$3$~and~$9$

$⇒$Odd multiple of~$2$~are

\left\{102, 106, 110, 114 \ldots \ldots . 998\right\}\left(225\text{numbers}\right)$

$⇒$No. of multiples of~$3$~are

\left\{102, 114, 126 \ldots \ldots . 990\right\}\left(75\text{numbers}\right)$

Which also include~multiple of~$9$

Hence, Required~$= 225 - 75 = 150$

questions.q: The number of $3$-digit odd numbers, whose sum of digits is a multiple of $7$, is _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the three-digit odd number be& $xyz$

Now~$z = 1 / 3 / 5 / 7 / 9$

$x + y + z = 7 / 14 / 21$~ [for sum of digit to be multiple of $7$]

$x + y = 6 / 4 / 2 / 13 / 11 / 9 / 7 / 5 / 20 / 18 / 16 / 14 / 12$

When~$x + y = 6 ⇒ \left(1, 5\right), \left(2, 4\right), \left($3, 3\right), \left(4, 2\right), \left(5, 1\right), \left(6, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 6$

When~$x + y = 4 ⇒ \left(1, 3\right), \left(2, 2\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(4, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 4$

When~$x + y = 2 ⇒ \left($1, 1\right), \left($2, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 2$

When~$x + y = 13 ⇒ \left($4, 9\right), \left($5, 8\right), \left($6, 7\right), \left(7, 6\right), \left(8, 5\right), \left(9, 4\right)$

Total possibilities$= 6$

When~$x + y = 11 ⇒ \left(2, 9\right), \left(3, 8\right), \left(4, 7\right), \left($5, 6\right), \left(6, 5\right), \left(6, 5\right), \left(7, 4\right), \left(8, 3\right), \left(9, 2\right)$

Total possibilities$= 8$

When~$x + y = 9 ⇒ \left(1, 8\right), \left(2, 7\right), \left(3, 8\right), \left(4, 5\right), \left($5, 4\right), \ldots . \left($8, 1\right), \left($9, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 9$

When~$x + y = 7 ⇒ \left($1, 8\right), \left(2, 5\right), \left(3, 4\right), \ldots . \left(8, 1\right), \left(7, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 7$

When~$x + y = 5 ⇒ \left(1, 4\right), \left(2, 3\right), \left(3, 2\right), \left(4, 1\right), \left(5, 0\right)$

Total possibilities$= 5$

When~$x + y = 20$ No~possibilities

When~$x + y = 18 ⇒ \left($9, 9\right)$

Total possibilities$= 1$

When~$x + y = 16 ⇒ \left($7, 9\right), \left(8, 8\right), \left(9, 7\right)$

Total possibilities$= 3$

When~$x + y = 14 ⇒ \left(5, 9\right), \left(6, 8\right), \left($7, 7\right), \left($8, 6\right), \left($9, 5\right)$

Total possibilities$= 5$

When~$x + y = 12 ⇒ \left($3, 9\right), \left(4, 8\right), \left(5, 7\right), \left(6, 6\right) \ldots . \left(9, 3\right)$

Total possibilities$= 7$

Hence, the total number of three digit~odd numbers whose sum of digit is divisible by~$7$~is~$63$

$

questions.q: The sum of all the four-digit numbers that can be formed using all the digits $2, 1, 2, 3$ is equal to ____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Total& $4$~digit numbers using the digits~$1, 2, 2, 3$~is

$= \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} = 12$

Numbers are

___3___3___3___2___2___2___2___2___2___1___1___1$

Required sum is

$= \mathop{\left[3 \times 3 + 2 \times 6 + 1 \times 3\right] ⏟}_{unitdigit ' ssum} + \mathop{\left[\left(3 \times 3 + 2 \times 6 + 1 \times 3\right) \times 10\right] ⏟}_{ten ' splacesum} + \mathop{\left[\left(3 \times 3 + 2 \times 6 + 1 \times 3\right) \times 100\right] ⏟}_{hundred ' splacesum} + \mathop{\left[\left(3 \times 3 + 2 \times 6 + 1 \times 3\right) \times 1000\right] ⏟}_{thousand ' splacesum}$

$= \left[24\right] + \left[$24 \times10\right] + \left[$24 \times100\right] + \left[$24 \times1000\right]$

$= 24 + 240 + 2400 + 24000 = 26664$

$
